title: The Fresh bread from the oven
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：fresh　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fresh 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the grandmother wrote of ① a fresh bread from the oven in the diary, and everybody in the courtyard said at once that it was ② fresher than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the grandmother, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the fresh ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the freshest bread from the oven anybody in the courtyard had ever seen, or so the diary for February 1946 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fresh to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the child who had come to help; the fresh ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fresh air from the hills, and said that no child in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fresh as the air from the hills they had once had in the old courtyard. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fresh or not, and he said so.

By 1959 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the diary. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fresh, and nothing besides. The child from the next courtyard called the whole plan ⑧ quite fresh; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the diary kept the names of the fresh ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1962, in public, she wrote of another fresh bread from the oven in the same diary, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ fresher than anybody had expected. ⑩ The freshest air from the hills in the whole courtyard, she said in 1964, was the one she could never quite name; the fresh ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 新鲜（前置定语 a fresh bread from the oven：1952 年祖母在日记里记下的那件新鲜的面包）
B. adj. 新鲜／清新（比较级 fresher than：文中两处，一处比刚出炉的面包，一处比预想）
C. adj. 新鲜／清新（最高级 the freshest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 新鲜（表语 too fresh to do：母亲觉得它太新鲜，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 清新（前置定语 a fresh air from the hills：叔叔把整件事称作一桩清新的空气）
F. adj. 清新（同级比较 as fresh as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩山里吹来的清新空气相比）
G. adj. 清新（后置定语 something fresh：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 清新（受程度副词修饰 quite fresh：那位孩子的评价）

items.q: a fresh bread from the oven
the freshest bread from the oven anybody
a fresh air from the hills
The freshest air from the hills in

answers.why: fresh 意为“新鲜”，1952 年祖母在日记里记下的是“一件新鲜的面包”，此处作前置定语 a fresh bread from the oven。
fresh 意为“新鲜”，此处用比较级 fresher than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fresh 意为“新鲜”，日记上 二月 那行字说它是院子里最新鲜的一件，故用最高级 the freshest bread from the oven。
fresh 意为“新鲜”，母亲认为这件东西“太新鲜了，谁也用不上”，too fresh to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fresh 意为“清新”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩清新的空气”，此处作前置定语 a fresh air from the hills。
fresh 意为“清新”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩山里吹来的清新空气一样清新”，同级比较用 as fresh as。
fresh 意为“清新”，日记上那半行字要的是“清新的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fresh。
fresh 意为“清新”，邻院子来的那位孩子认为这套计划“相当清新”，quite 修饰原级 fresh。
fresh 意为“清新”，1962 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要清新”，故用比较级 fresher than。
fresh 意为“清新”，母亲 1964 年说的是“整个院子里最清新的那一桩”，故用最高级 the freshest air from the hills。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年，祖母在日记里记下了一件新鲜的面包。（a fresh bread from the oven）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更新鲜。（fresher than …）
母亲觉得它太新鲜，谁也用不上。（too fresh to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩清新的空气。（a fresh air from the hills）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩山里吹来的清新空气一样清新。（as fresh as …）
到了 1959 年，日记上只剩半行字：要的是一件清新的东西。（something fresh）
answers: In 1952 the grandmother wrote of a fresh bread from the oven in the diary.
Everybody said it was fresher than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too fresh to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a fresh air from the hills.
He said nobody would call it as fresh as the air from the hills they had once had.
By 1959 the diary asked for nothing but something fresh.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fresh 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the grandmother wrote of a fresh bread from the oven in the diary, and nobody forgot it.
It was the freshest bread from the oven in the courtyard, or so the diary says.
My mother thought it too fresh to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a fresh air from the hills, and nobody argued with him.
The child from the next courtyard called the plan quite fresh, and everybody laughed.
The fresh ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
